text:
incident-bot: PAGER — SRE oncall (Jordan) — High GPU backlog and 5xx spike in eu-west-1. Alert group: inference-throughput. Autoescalate in 5m unless acked.

Jordan: acked — looking now. saw 502s and queue length grow.

Jordan: initial check: autoscaler-controller v2.4.1 not scaling pools fast enough, some preemptions on spot nodes.

Alex: @Jordan which pools?

Jordan: eu-w1-gpu-pool-3 and eu-w1-gpu-pool-4. GPU util ~98%, pending queue ~34k tokens requests count ~4200.

Maria: tagging product impact — some hosted customers experienced timeouts and streaming cutoffs. Not seeing data loss but timeouts. 

Samir: can we fallback to smaller model variant or CPU fallback for non-low-latency routes?

Jordan: initiating partial routing to cheaper variants for non-interactive endpoints. Pushing routing rule: 
```
POST /v1/routing/policy/apply
{ "route": "hosted/*/batch", "policy": "fallback-to-variant:small-v2", "weight": 0.3 }
```

Kelly: applied 0.3 throttle. Observing ~10% reduction in token pressure. Good.

Alex: I'm going to bump Dedicated pool min_replicas for eu-w1-gpu-pool-3 to add 2 nodes (hot spare). Doing resize now.

eng-platform-bot: resize job submitted: job_id=resize-9872, target_add=2, expected_ready=3m

Jordan: also enabling emergency-burst capacity in dedicated for affected accounts (per runbook). @Alex confirm policy ID.

Alex: policy ID: RB-EMER-3. Triggered.

Samir: autoscaler logs snippet: 
```
[12:31:02] scale_decision: target= +1, cooldown=120s
[12:31:45] scale_rejected: insufficient spare instances in region
[12:32:10] spot_preempt: node eu-w1-spot-12 terminated
```

Jordan: preemption pattern causing oscillation. We need to mark some nodes as on-demand or reserve.

Maria: Customer comms — I posted a short note in status.redwood.ai and flagged the top 3 customers likely affected. Will draft follow-up email once we know root cause.

Kelly: observed 502 rate dropping after resize and fallback routing — 502s -> 1.8% from 6.2% in 7m. Latency p50 improved by 180ms.

Jordan: good. I'll do an on-call handoff at T+40 to @Alex for remediation work and tracking.

Alex: taking over oncall. Jordan, leaving notes: watch autoscaler cooldown and avoid simultaneous scale-downs.

Jordan: notes left in /incidents/1823507890/hand-off.md (private). quick list: 
- primary: bump min_replicas for eu-w1 pools
- short-term: reserve 4 on-demand instances in eu-west-1
- medium: adjust autoscaler policy to prefer less aggressive downscale for gpu pools

Samir: suggests follow-up action: add neural-network-model variants with smaller kv-cache so they can run on CPU in emergencies. Filed as action 1.

Alex: creating remediation tracking ticket: INFRA-6389. I'll assign owners and ETA.

Alex: action items and owners (quick):
- INFRA-6389: Reserve on-demand instances for eu-west-1 across high-traffic pools — owner: Alex — ETA: 2026-03-19
- INFRA-6390: Autoscaler tuning: longer downscale cooldown & add preemption-aware backoff — owner: Maria — ETA: 2026-03-22
- INFRA-6391: Add CPU-fallback route and smaller model build for batch endpoints — owner: Samir — ETA: 2026-03-26
- INFRA-6392: Postmortem writeup & customer impact assessment — owner: Jordan — ETA: 2026-03-18

Kelly: adding monitoring alerts to watch for surge >85% GPU util for 3 consecutive mins and pending queue >10k.

eng-platform-bot: post-incident checklist reminder: schedule postmortem within 72h, assign follow-ups, link runbook.

Jordan: scheduling postmortem: Wed 2026-03-18 10:00 UTC. Invites sent to SRE, Eng-Infra, Product, and Solutions.

Maria: I'll present customer impact and timeline in the postmortem.

Samir: will include model-variant fallback design notes.

Alex: will bring infra cost/commitment trade-offs for reserving on-demand capacity.

Kelly: I'll update dashboards and add token-level costs for fallback routing so we can quantify unit economics.

Jordan: quick RCA notes (preliminary): root cause = combination of spot preemptions in eu-west reducing available GPU capacity + autoscaler cooldown logic that under-reacted to rapid sustained load spike; secondary: some older kernel builds had higher memory pressure increasing evictions.

Samir: flagged kernel build v1.8.3 on eu-w1-gpu-pool-3. Need to schedule rolling update postmortem.

Alex: for remediation, propose: 1) short-term reserve 4 on-demand, 2) autoscaler tuning, 3) add fair-share queueing when pending tokens exceed threshold.

Jordan: agree. Also add test scenarios to chaos tests: simulate spot preemptions during sustained ramp. Filed INFRA-6393. Owner: Kelly. ETA 2026-03-30.

Maria: customer follow-ups: send timeline + mitigation summary by end of day. I'll coordinate with CS.

Kelly: reaction :thumbsup: to timeline.

Alex: closing loop — current status: degraded -> recovering -> service green in region. Will update ticket INFRA-6389 with progress.

Jordan: leaving final note before handoff: keep monitoring for 2 hours; escalate to exec if we see repeat within 24h.

Samir: reassigning a couple of follow-ups in tracker.

eng-platform-bot: incident closed by Alex at 1823508265. Postmortem scheduled at 182395? (see calendar invite).

Jordan: thanks team — nice quick mitigation. We'll make sure remediation tickets are tracked and the postmortem covers runbook gaps. :coffee:
